sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā sumahānādaṃ bhīmasenasya dhanvinaḥ babhūva paramā prītir dharmarājasya saṃyuge
english: Hearing that mighty roar of Bhīmasena the bowman, the Dharmarāja was filled with the highest joy in the battle.

sanskrit: tato hṛṣṭo mahārāja vāditrāṇāṃ mahāsvanaiḥ bhīmasenaravaṃ pārthaḥ pratijagrāha sarvaśaḥ
english: Then, O great king, the delighted Pārtha answered Bhīmasena's roar on every side with the loud blare of musical instruments.

sanskrit: abhyayāc caiva samare droṇam astrabhṛtāṃ varam harṣeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ kṛtasaṃjñe vṛkodare
english: And when Vṛkodara had given the signal, filled with great gladness he advanced in the battle against Droṇa, the foremost of weapon-bearers.

sanskrit: ekatriṃśan mahārāja putrāṃs tava mahārathān hatān duryodhano dṛṣṭvā kṣattuḥ sasmāra tad vacaḥ
english: Seeing thirty-one of your sons, great car-warriors all, slain, O great king, Duryodhana remembered those words of Vidura the steward.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ kṣattur hitakaraṃ vacaḥ iti saṃcintya rājāsau nottaraṃ pratyapadyata
english: "Now has come to pass that beneficial word of the steward,"—so reflecting, that king found no answer to make.

sanskrit: yad dyūtakāle durbuddhir abravīt tanayas tava yac ca karṇo 'bravīt kṛṣṇāṃ sabhāyāṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ
english: What your evil-minded son had spoken at the time of the dice-game, and the harsh words that Karṇa had spoken to Kṛṣṇā in the assembly—

sanskrit: pramukhe pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tava caiva viśāṃ pate kauravāṇāṃ ca sarveṣām ācāryasya ca saṃnidhau
english: in the presence of the sons of Pāṇḍu, and of yourself, O lord of peoples, and of all the Kauravas, and in the very presence of the preceptor—

sanskrit: vinaṣṭāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kṛṣṇe śāśvataṃ narakaṃ gatāḥ patim anyaṃ vṛṇīṣveti tasyedaṃ phalam āgatam
english: "The Pāṇḍavas are utterly ruined, O Kṛṣṇā; they have gone to everlasting hell. Choose yourself another husband"—the fruit of that has now arrived.

sanskrit: yat sma tāṃ paruṣāṇy āhuḥ sabhām ānāyya draupadīm pāṇḍavān ugradhanuṣaḥ krodhayantas tavātmajāḥ
english: When, having brought Draupadī into the assembly, they spoke harsh words to her, your sons enraged the Pāṇḍavas of terrible bows.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ krodhāgniṃ trayodaśa samāḥ sthitam visṛjaṃs tava putrāṇām antaṃ gacchati kaurava
english: Loosing that fire of wrath which had abided in him thirteen years, Bhīmasena, O Kaurava, is bringing your sons to their end.

sanskrit: vilapaṃś ca bahu kṣattā śamaṃ nālabhata tvayi saputro bharataśreṣṭha tasya bhuṅkṣva phalodayam hato vikarṇo rājendra citrasenaś ca vīryavān
english: Lamenting much, the steward could find no peace with you, O best of the Bhāratas, you together with your sons; now reap the ripening of that fruit. Vikarṇa is slain, O lord of kings, and valiant Citrasena too.

sanskrit: pravarān ātmajānāṃ te sutāṃś cānyān mahārathān yān yāṃś ca dadṛśe bhīmaś cakṣurviṣayam āgatān putrāṃs tava mahābāho tvarayā tāñ jaghāna ha
english: The foremost among your sons, and other of your sons, great car-warriors—whomever Bhīma saw come within range of his eye, those sons of yours, O mighty-armed one, he slew in haste.

sanskrit: tvatkṛte hy aham adrākṣaṃ dahyamānāṃ varūthinīm sahasraśaḥ śarair muktaiḥ pāṇḍavena vṛṣeṇa ca
english: On your account I have beheld the host consumed as if by fire, by the arrows loosed in their thousands by the Pāṇḍava and by the Bull Karṇa.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca mahān apanayaḥ sūta mamaivātra viśeṣataḥ sa idānīm anuprāpto manye saṃjaya śocataḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Great was the misgovernance, O charioteer, mine above all herein; that has now come home, I think, O Saṃjaya, to me who grieve.

sanskrit: yad gataṃ tad gatam iti mamāsīn manasi sthitam idānīm atra kiṃ kāryaṃ prakariṣyāmi saṃjaya
english: "What is gone is gone"—this was fixed in my mind; now what is to be done here, what shall I do, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: yathā tv eṣa kṣayo vṛtto mamāpanayasaṃbhavaḥ vīrāṇāṃ tan mamācakṣva sthirībhūto 'smi saṃjaya
english: But how this destruction of heroes, born of my own misrule, came to pass—tell me that; I have grown steady, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇabhīmau mahārāja parākrāntau mahāhave bāṇavarṣāṇy avarṣetāṃ vṛṣṭimantāv ivāmbudau
english: Saṃjaya said: Karṇa and Bhīma, O great king, putting forth their valour in the great battle, rained down showers of arrows like two rain-laden clouds.

sanskrit: bhīmanāmāṅkitā bāṇāḥ svarṇapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ viviśuḥ karṇam āsādya bhindanta iva jīvitam
english: Arrows marked with Bhīma's name, golden-feathered and whetted on stone, reaching Karṇa entered him as though cleaving his very life.

sanskrit: tathaiva karṇanirmuktaiḥ saviṣair iva pannagaiḥ ākīryata raṇe bhīmaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Even so was Bhīma covered in the fight, by hundreds and by thousands, with the shafts loosed from Karṇa, like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: tayoḥ śarair mahārāja saṃpatadbhiḥ samantataḥ babhūva tava sainyānāṃ saṃkṣobhaḥ sāgaropamaḥ
english: From the arrows of those two falling on every side, O great king, there arose among your armies a tumult like that of the ocean.

sanskrit: bhīmacāpacyutair bāṇais tava sainyam ariṃdama avadhyata camūmadhye ghorair āśīviṣopamaiḥ
english: By the arrows loosed from Bhīma's bow, O subduer of foes, your army was slaughtered in the midst of the host—dreadful shafts, the likeness of snakes of deadly poison.

sanskrit: vāraṇaiḥ patitai rājan vājibhiś ca naraiḥ saha adṛśyata mahī kīrṇā vātanunnair drumair iva
english: Strewn with fallen elephants, O king, and with horses and men together, the earth appeared as if littered with trees uprooted by the wind.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare bhīmacāpacyutaiḥ śaraiḥ prādravaṃs tāvakā yodhāḥ kim etad iti cābruvan
english: Being slain in the battle by the arrows loosed from Bhīma's bow, your warriors fled, crying out, "What is this?"

sanskrit: tato vyudastaṃ tat sainyaṃ sindhusauvīrakauravam protsāritaṃ mahāvegaiḥ karṇapāṇḍavayoḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then that army of the Sindhus, the Sauvīras, and the Kauravas was scattered and driven off by the swift arrows of Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: te śarāturabhūyiṣṭhā hatāśvanaravāhanāḥ utsṛjya karṇaṃ bhīmaṃ ca prādravan sarvatodiśam
english: Sore wounded with arrows for the most part, their horses, men, and mounts slain, they abandoned Karṇa and Bhīma and fled in every direction.

sanskrit: nūnaṃ pārthārtham evāsmān mohayanti divaukasaḥ yat karṇabhīmaprabhavair vadhyate no balaṃ śaraiḥ
english: "Surely for Pārtha's sake the dwellers of heaven bewilder us, in that our host is being slain by the arrows that spring from Karṇa and Bhīma."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvanto yodhās te tāvakā bhayapīḍitāḥ śarapātaṃ samutsṛjya sthitā yuddhadidṛkṣavaḥ
english: Speaking thus, your warriors, oppressed by fear, withdrew beyond arrow-range and stood there, eager only to watch the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāvartata nadī ghorarūpā mahāhave babhūva ca viśeṣeṇa bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhinī
english: Then there flowed, in that great battle, a river of dreadful aspect, which especially heightened the terror of the timorous.

sanskrit: vāraṇāśvamanuṣyāṇāṃ rudhiraughasamudbhavā saṃvṛtā gatasattvaiś ca manuṣyagajavājibhiḥ
english: It rose from the streaming blood of elephants, horses, and men, and was thronged with lifeless men, elephants, and steeds.

sanskrit: sānukarṣapatākaiś ca dvipāśvarathabhūṣaṇaiḥ syandanair apaviddhaiś ca bhagnacakrākṣakūbaraiḥ
english: With the trappings of elephants, horses, and cars, with their axle-poles and banners, and with chariots cast aside, their wheels, axles, and shafts broken—

sanskrit: jātarūpapariṣkārair dhanurbhiḥ sumahādhanaiḥ suvarṇapuṅkhair iṣubhir nārācaiś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: with bows adorned with gold and of exceeding worth, with golden-feathered shafts, and with iron arrows by the thousand—

sanskrit: karṇapāṇḍavanirmuktair nirmuktair iva pannagaiḥ prāsatomarasaṃghātaiḥ khaḍgaiś ca saparaśvadhaiḥ
english: loosed by Karṇa and the Pāṇḍava like serpents set free, with masses of darts and lances, with swords and battle-axes—

sanskrit: suvarṇavikṛtaiś cāpi gadāmusalapaṭṭiśaiḥ vajraiś ca vividhākāraiḥ śaktibhiḥ parighair api śataghnībhiś ca citrābhir babhau bhārata medinī
english: and with maces, clubs, and spiked spears wrought with gold, with thunderbolt-darts of many shapes, with spears and bludgeons, and with gleaming hundred-slayers, the earth shone bright, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kanakāṅgadakeyūraiḥ kuṇḍalair maṇibhiḥ śubhaiḥ tanutraiḥ satalatraiś ca hārair niṣkaiś ca bhārata
english: With golden armlets and bracelets, with earrings and shining gems, with coats of mail and with hand-guards, with necklaces and ornaments of gold, O Bhārata—

sanskrit: vastraiś chatraiś ca vidhvastaiś cāmaravyajanair api gajāśvamanujair bhinnaiḥ śastraiḥ syandanabhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: with garments and parasols torn asunder, with yak-tail whisks and fans, with the cleft bodies of elephants, horses, and men, with weapons and the trappings of chariots—

sanskrit: tais taiś ca vividhair bhāvais tatra tatra vasuṃdharā patitair apaviddhaiś ca saṃbabhau dyaur iva grahaiḥ
english: with these manifold objects of every kind, fallen and flung about here and there, the earth shone like the firmament with its planets.

sanskrit: acintyam adbhutaṃ caiva tayoḥ karmātimānuṣam dṛṣṭvā cāraṇasiddhānāṃ vismayaḥ samapadyata
english: Beholding the unimaginable, wondrous, and more-than-human deeds of those two, amazement seized the Cāraṇas and the Siddhas.

sanskrit: agner vāyusahāyasya gatiḥ kakṣa ivāhave āsīd bhīmasahāyasya raudram ādhirather gatam nipātitadhvajarathaṃ hatavājinaradvipam
english: As fire aided by the wind sweeps through dry brushwood, so was the course in battle of the son of Adhiratha, having Bhīma for his match; terrible was that course, casting down banners and cars and slaying horses, men, and elephants.

sanskrit: gajābhyāṃ saṃprayuktābhyām āsīn naḍavanaṃ yathā tathābhūtaṃ mahat sainyam āsīd bhārata saṃyuge vimardaḥ karṇabhīmābhyām āsīc ca paramo raṇe
english: As a thicket of reeds is crushed by two elephants joined in combat, so was that great army brought low in the battle, O Bhārata; and supreme was the havoc wrought by Karṇa and Bhīma in the fight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tataḥ karṇo mahārāja bhīmaṃ viddhvā tribhiḥ śaraiḥ mumoca śaravarṣāṇi citrāṇi ca bahūni ca
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Karṇa, O great king, having pierced Bhīma with three shafts, loosed showers of arrows, brilliant and manifold.

sanskrit: vadhyamāno mahārāja sūtaputreṇa pāṇḍavaḥ na vivyathe bhīmaseno bhidyamāna ivācalaḥ
english: Though smitten by the son of the charioteer, O great king, the Pāṇḍava Bhīmasena did not waver, like a mountain being riven.

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ karṇinā karṇe pītena niśitena ca vivyādha yudhi rājendra bhīmasenaḥ patatriṇā
english: Then Bhīmasena, O lord of kings, pierced Karṇa in the ear with a barbed, whetted, yellow-hued, feathered shaft in the fight.

sanskrit: sa kuṇḍalaṃ mahat karṇāt karṇasyāpātayad bhuvi tapanīyaṃ mahārāja dīptaṃ jyotir ivāmbarāt
english: He struck the great earring of refined gold from Karṇa's ear to the ground, O great king, like a blazing light falling from the sky.

sanskrit: athāpareṇa bhallena sūtaputraṃ stanāntare ājaghāna bhṛśaṃ bhīmaḥ smayann iva mahābalaḥ
english: Then with another broad-headed arrow the mighty Bhīma, as if smiling, struck the charioteer's son hard between the breasts.

sanskrit: punar asya tvaran bhīmo nārācān daśa bhārata raṇe praiṣīn mahāvegān yamadaṇḍopamāṃs tathā
english: Then again, in haste, Bhīma sped at him in the battle ten iron arrows of great swiftness, O Bhārata, like the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: te lalāṭaṃ samāsādya sūtaputrasya māriṣa viviśuś coditās tena valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Reaching the forehead of the charioteer's son, O sire, those arrows, driven by him, entered it as serpents enter an ant-hill.

sanskrit: lalāṭasthais tu tair bāṇaiḥ sūtaputro vyarocata nīlotpalamayīṃ mālāṃ dhārayan sa purā yathā
english: With those arrows fixed in his forehead the charioteer's son shone forth, as he had of old when wearing a garland wrought of blue lotuses.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe karṇaḥ pīḍito dṛḍhadhanvanā vegaṃ cakre mahāvego bhīmasenavadhaṃ prati
english: Then Karṇa, enraged in the fight, sore pressed by the strong bowman, mighty in speed, put forth his swiftness to slay Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tasmai karṇaḥ śataṃ rājann iṣūṇāṃ gārdhravāsasām amarṣī balavān kruddhaḥ preṣayām āsa bhārata
english: At him Karṇa, O king, impatient, strong, and wrathful, sped a hundred arrows feathered with vulture-plumes, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāsṛjad ugrāṇi śaravarṣāṇi pāṇḍavaḥ samare tam anādṛtya nāsya vīryam acintayat
english: Then the Pāṇḍava loosed fierce showers of arrows; heeding him not in the battle, he gave no thought to his prowess.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇo mahārāja pāṇḍavaṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghānorasi kruddhaḥ kruddharūpaṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then Karṇa, O great king, that scorcher of foes, in his wrath struck the wrathful-looking Pāṇḍava upon the breast with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: jīmūtāv iva cānyonyaṃ tau vavarṣatur āhave talaśabdaravaiś caiva trāsayantau parasparam
english: Like two storm-clouds they rained upon each other in the battle, terrifying one another with the cracking sounds of their bow-strings.

sanskrit: śarajālaiś ca vividhaiś chādayām āsatur mṛdhe anyonyaṃ samare kruddhau kṛtapratikṛtaiṣiṇau
english: With manifold nets of arrows they covered each other in the fray, both wrathful in the battle, each seeking to repay deed with deed.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhū rādheyasya mahātmanaḥ kṣurapreṇa dhanuś chittvā karṇaṃ vivyādha patriṇā
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīma, having cut the bow of the high-souled Rādheya with a razor-tipped arrow, pierced Karṇa with a feathered shaft.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ sūtaputro mahāmanāḥ anyat kārmukam ādatta vegaghnaṃ bhārasādhanam
english: Casting aside that severed bow, the high-minded son of the charioteer took up another, swift-striking and able to bear a heavy strain.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca kurusauvīrasaindhavānāṃ balakṣayam savarmadhvajaśastraiś ca patitaiḥ saṃvṛtāṃ mahīm
english: And seeing the destruction of the host of the Kurus, the Sauvīras, and the Saindhavas, and the earth covered with fallen armour, banners, and weapons—

sanskrit: hastyaśvanaradehāṃś ca gatāsūn prekṣya sarvataḥ sūtaputrasya saṃrambhād dīptaṃ vapur ajāyata
english: and beholding on every side the lifeless bodies of elephants, horses, and men, the form of the charioteer's son grew blazing with fury.

sanskrit: sa visphārya mahac cāpaṃ kārtasvaravibhūṣitam bhīmaṃ praikṣata rādheyo rājan ghoreṇa cakṣuṣā
english: Twanging his great bow adorned with gold, Rādheya gazed upon Bhīma, O king, with a terrible eye.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddhaḥ śarān asyan sūtaputro vyarocata madhyaṃdinagato 'rciṣmāñ śaradīva divākaraḥ
english: Then the wrathful son of the charioteer, hurling his shafts, shone forth radiant like the autumn sun risen to the meridian.

sanskrit: marīcivikacasyeva rājan bhānumato vapuḥ āsīd ādhirather ghoraṃ vapuḥ śaraśatārciṣaḥ
english: Like the form of the sun blossoming with its rays, O king, was the dreadful form of the son of Adhiratha, ablaze with hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: karābhyām ādadānasya saṃdadhānasya cāśugān vikarṣato muñcato vā nāntaraṃ dadṛśū raṇe
english: As he took up his swift shafts with both hands, set them to the string, drew them back, and loosed them, none in the battle could mark the interval.

sanskrit: agnicakropamaṃ ghoraṃ maṇḍalīkṛtam āyudham karṇasyāsīn mahārāja savyadakṣiṇam asyataḥ
english: As he discharged his shafts to the left and to the right, the weapon of Karṇa, O great king, dreadful as a wheel of fire, seemed drawn into a circle.

sanskrit: svarṇapuṅkhāḥ suniśitāḥ karṇacāpacyutāḥ śarāḥ prācchādayan mahārāja diśaḥ sūryasya ca prabhām
english: Golden-feathered and well-whetted, the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow veiled, O great king, the quarters and the splendour of the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhānāṃ śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām dhanuścyutānāṃ viyati dadṛśe bahudhā vrajaḥ
english: Then in the sky was seen, in manifold array, a flight of gold-feathered arrows with smooth-bending joints, loosed from his bow.

sanskrit: śarāsanād ādhiratheḥ prabhavantaḥ sma sāyakāḥ śreṇīkṛtā vyarājanta rājan krauñcā ivāmbare
english: Issuing from the bow of the son of Adhiratha, the shafts, ranged in lines, shone forth, O king, like cranes in the heavens.

sanskrit: gārdhrapatrāñ śilādhautān kārtasvaravibhūṣitān mahāvegān pradīptāgrān mumocādhirathiḥ śarān
english: Vulture-feathered, stone-whetted, adorned with gold, of great swiftness and blazing points—such arrows did the son of Adhiratha loose.

sanskrit: te tu cāpabaloddhūtāḥ śātakumbhavibhūṣitāḥ ajasram anvakīryanta śarāḥ pārtharathaṃ prati
english: Hurled by the force of the bow and decked with gold, those arrows poured ceaselessly upon the chariot of Pārtha's son Bhīma.

sanskrit: te vyomni ratnavikṛtā vyakāśanta sahasraśaḥ śalabhānām iva vrātāḥ śarāḥ karṇasamīritāḥ
english: Gem-wrought, they shone in the sky by the thousand—the arrows sped by Karṇa, like swarms of locusts.

sanskrit: cāpād ādhirather muktāḥ prapatantaḥ sma sāyakāḥ eko dīrgha iva prāṃśuḥ prabhavan dṛśyate śaraḥ
english: Loosed from the bow of the son of Adhiratha, the falling shafts seemed, as they sped forth, to be a single long and towering arrow.

sanskrit: parvataṃ vāridhārābhiś chādayann iva toyadaḥ karṇaḥ prācchādayat kruddho bhīmaṃ sāyakavṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: As a rain-cloud veils a mountain with its torrents, so did the wrathful Karṇa cover Bhīma with showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata bhīmasya balavīryaparākramam vyavasāyaṃ ca putrās te praikṣanta kurubhiḥ saha
english: There, O Bhārata, your sons together with the Kurus beheld the strength, the valour, the prowess, and the resolve of Bhīma.

sanskrit: tāṃ samudram ivoddhūtāṃ śaravṛṣṭiṃ samutthitām acintayitvā bhīmas tu kruddhaḥ karṇam upādravat
english: Heedless of that risen shower of arrows, swollen like the surging sea, the wrathful Bhīma rushed upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: rukmapṛṣṭhaṃ mahac cāpaṃ bhīmasyāsīd viśāṃ pate ākarṣān maṇḍalībhūtaṃ śakracāpam ivāparam tasmāc charāḥ prādurāsan pūrayanta ivāmbaram
english: The great gold-backed bow of Bhīma, O lord of peoples, drawn into a circle by his pull, seemed a second rainbow of Indra; from it the arrows came forth as if filling the firmament.

sanskrit: suvarṇapuṅkhair bhīmena sāyakair nataparvabhiḥ gagane racitā mālā kāñcanīva vyarājata
english: By the gold-feathered, smooth-jointed shafts of Bhīma there was wrought in the sky a garland that shone as if of gold.

sanskrit: tato vyomni viṣaktāni śarajālāni bhāgaśaḥ āhatāni vyaśīryanta bhīmasenasya patribhiḥ
english: Then the nets of arrows clinging in the sky, struck piece by piece by the feathered shafts of Bhīmasena, were scattered asunder.

sanskrit: karṇasya śarajālaughair bhīmasenasya cobhayoḥ agnisphuliṅgasaṃsparśair añjogatibhir āhave tais taiḥ kanakapuṅkhānāṃ dyaur āsīt saṃvṛtā vrajaiḥ
english: By the floods of arrow-nets of both Karṇa and Bhīmasena, touching like sparks of fire and flying straight in the battle, the sky was wholly covered with flights of gold-feathered shafts.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ chādayan bāṇaiḥ sūtaputraḥ pṛthagvidhaiḥ upārohad anādṛtya tasya vīryaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Covering Bhīma with arrows of many kinds, the charioteer's son pressed upon him, making light of the prowess of that high-souled one.

sanskrit: tayor visṛjatos tatra śarajālāni māriṣa vāyubhūtāny adṛśyanta saṃsaktānītaretaram
english: As those two there loosed their nets of arrows, O sire, they seemed to become like winds, clashing one against the other.

sanskrit: tasmai karṇaḥ śitān bāṇān karmāraparimārjitān suvarṇavikṛtān kruddhaḥ prāhiṇod vadhakāṅkṣayā
english: At him Karṇa, in his wrath, sped sharp arrows burnished by the smith and wrought with gold, longing to slay him.

sanskrit: tān antarikṣe viśikhais tridhaikaikam aśātayat viśeṣayan sūtaputraṃ bhīmas tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Those Bhīma cut down in mid-air with his shafts, each into three, and outdoing the charioteer's son he cried, "Stand and fight!"
